rich_summary: At Rama’s great sacrificial gathering, sages, kings, monkeys, titans, and people of every rank assemble to witness a decisive moment: Sita’s public oath of innocence. The immense crowd waits in tense silence until the sage Valmiki arrives, leading Sita. She walks behind him with bowed head and folded palms, overcome with grief yet inwardly fixed on Rama. The sight of the wronged queen moves the entire assembly to cries of sorrow and praise for both Rama and Sita. Valmiki then addresses Rama directly, declaring Sita’s virtue and explaining that she had been abandoned near his hermitage because of public slander. He announces that she will prove her purity and reveals that the twin boys raised in his care are Rama’s own sons. The scene prepares for a dramatic vindication of Sita before the whole world.

top_scenes.scene_text: Valmiki solemnly leads the sorrowful Sita with bowed head and folded palms into a vast sacrificial arena crowded with sages, kings, monkeys, and celestial beings.
The immense assembly erupts in cries of grief and reverence as Sita appears behind Valmiki, the crowd shouting 'Halahala!' while others hail Rama and Sita.
Valmiki stands before Rama in the royal sacrificial court, declaring Sita’s purity and revealing that the twin boys raised in his hermitage are Rama’s sons.
